title: Inverse image preserves finite constant ring tower limits
statement: For every morphism of schemes f:X→Y and every countable inverse system Q of finite commutative rings in the sheaf-value universe, the ring-valued pro-etale inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves the limit of the diagram of constant ring sheaves Q on Y. Transition maps need not be surjective.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf, and Tag 00YV, lemma-morphism-of-sites-algebraic-structures; proetale.tex Tag 098T (2).

proof.text: Choose the representing diagram and cone furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-tower-representation]. Yoneda sends each of its two geometric limit cones to a limiting sheaf cone.

The inverse image of a lifted representable is the lifted representable of its base change: combine Mathlib compULiftYonedaIsoULiftYonedaCompLan with the sheafification counit. Transfer preservation through this natural isomorphism and through the representing-diagram isomorphism.

The ring forgetful functor commutes with inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-pullback-forget-comparison]: its required Kan extensions are filtered because base change is representably flat, and forgetting commutative rings preserves filtered colimits. Forgetting also commutes with sheafification.

Forgetting ring-sheaf structure preserves and reflects limits, as checked after the fully faithful inclusion into presheaves. Compose the preserved set-valued cone with this comparison and reflect its limiting property back to ring sheaves.
